object_description: T-shaped building composition with expressive sports cube
design_condition: The building sets its longitudinal structure back from the street, forms a small courtyard, and uses a raised sports volume to create a strong urban figure beside the neighbouring buildings.

positive.statement: The project proposes a remarkably idiosyncratic composition of perpendicular wall panels and two fields.
The expressive sports figure gains enough strength for the relatively small building to assert itself independently in the urban space.
The setbacks and contrasting building shapes nevertheless create volumetric unity.
The atrium and central organization create surprisingly new spatial experiences within a familiar corridor arrangement.
The school wing structure is functional, efficient, and easy to implement.
The project achieves a strong urban-development response and a spatially convincing school proposal.

negative.statement: The small courtyard and differentiated planting, lounge, and hedge areas are unlikely to be robust enough for the site.
The courtyard is hardly suitable as a publicly usable neighbourhood space.
The open arrangement of the kiosk is an operational disadvantage.
The classroom dimensions are at the lower limit and the exposed collections restrict usability and flexibility.
The front glazing of the gymnasiums and the equipment-room design may restrict sports use.
The sports supporting structure is not convincing conceptually or technically, particularly because of deformation and vibration behaviour.
The very large sports-hall windows increase cooling demand and the risk of summer overheating.
The building violates the applicable building regulations despite moving away from the construction line.
The below-average space efficiency, oversized basement, and atrium fire-protection requirements lead to poor economic efficiency.
